uncited: *   **Inputs:** Light source spectral power distribution $L(\lambda)$, viewing direction $\omega$, sampling position $x$, entry point $d$ (where the light ray first enters the volume), distance $D = |x - d|$, spectral extinction coefficient $\tau(x, \lambda)$, and local material reflectance properties for the Phong model.
*   Spectral extinction coefficient $\tau(x, \lambda)$: Defined per voxel and wavelength.
*   Local material reflectance: Parameters for the Phong model (ambient, diffuse, specular coefficients).
Determine the entry point $d$ where the light ray first intersects the volume boundary for the given direction $\omega$.
Calculate the distance $D$ from the sampling position $x$ to the entry point $d$.
Evaluate the spectral extinction integral $\int_0^s \tau(x-t\omega, \lambda) dt$ for $s$ ranging from $0$ to $D$.
This is typically discretized along the ray segment from $d$ to $x$.
Compute the transmission $T(x, \omega, \lambda, s)$ using the exponential of the negative extinction integral.
Compute the scattered radiance $\tilde{I}_r$ at each point along the ray using the local Phong illumination model.
Evaluate the integral $\int_0^D \tilde{I}_r(x - s\omega, \omega, \lambda) \cdot T(x, \omega, \lambda, s) ds$ using numerical quadrature (e.g., trapezoidal rule) over the sampled points.
Compute the boundary term $\tilde{I}_i(x - D\omega, \omega, \lambda) \cdot T(x, \omega, \lambda, D)$.
Since the ray enters at $d$, $\tilde{I}_i(x - D\omega, \omega, \lambda)$ represents the irradiance just outside the volume, which is typically $L(\lambda)$ or 0 if no light is present.
Sum the boundary term and the integral result to get $\tilde{I}_i(x, \omega, \lambda)$.
Multiply by the light source spectral power $L(\lambda)$ to obtain the final irradiance $I_i(x, \omega, \lambda)$.
*   Phong parameters ($k_a, k_d, k_s, shininess$): Material-specific.
Use clamping or log-space arithmetic if necessary.
If the ray does not enter the volume, the result is zero.

The spectral precomputation variant uses an array of 4D textures, which can be memory-intensive.
